ledger.claim: The four conditions in POL-NS-01 are conjunctive, and the rider wins by breaking any one of them. The driver's own GPS trace measures a single continuous in-geofence hold from 17:15:00 to 17:19:00 — 240 seconds — against the 300 seconds limb (c) requires for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, a shortfall of 60 seconds. The dwell condition therefore fails, the cancellation fee of SGD 8.00 is not chargeable, and the trip record's own figures agree: arrived 17:15:20, cancelled 17:19:00, a wait of 3.7 minutes.

POL-NS-06 makes this a strict-liability shortfall, not a fault contest: where the effective in-geofence dwell falls below the POL-NS-01 minimum for the zone class, the cancellation fee is refunded in full 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages'. The measured dwell is 240 seconds against a 300-second minimum, so the whole contested SGD 8.00 is refundable to the rider.

The driver cannot repair the shortfall by summing intervals under POL-NS-06(i): the trace shows exactly one in-geofence interval (run_count 1), so there is no second interval to add to the first. In fairness I disclose that the traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-09103-01 is MISSING on the pre-pass, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0 — no advisory covers this pickup road and waiting window, and a MISSING artifact can carry no fact — so limb (i) has nothing to operate on in any event.

I do not press POL-NS-05, and the rider's case does not need it. The record shows no false arrival marker: at the 'arrived' timestamp of 17:15:20 the trace places the driver about 24 m from the pin and stationary (the only distinct speed on the driver track is 0.0 kph), so neither the 300 m nor the 15 kph trigger is met. The point is outcome-neutral anyway — on the POL-NS-05 recomputation the waiting clock starts at the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 17:15:00, and the corrected dwell is still 240 seconds, still 60 short.

I concede that POL-NS-04 cannot be run on this record: the chat log contains no rider message at all — its three messages are one system 'Your driver has arrived' notice and two driver messages — so limb (a) fails, and the rider's own track sits 519 m from the pin with zero qualifying fixes, so limb (c) fails as well. That concession costs the rider nothing here, because POL-NS-06 conditions the refund on the driver's dwell, not on the rider's presence or her responsiveness; the rider's claimed narrative is not that she was ignored, but that the driver cancelled before the waiting period was up.

I do not allege a fare defect, because there is none: SGD 8.00 is the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00), which is exactly what the fare breakdown records, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. Nor is anything impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d): the driver 'arrived' event at 17:15:20 sits on a GPS fix at the same instant, the trace carries 25 fixes with a maximum gap of 0 seconds across the 17:15:00-17:19:00 window, and the chat holds precisely the 3 messages trip_record.chat_message_count reports. The bundle is clean and the case is decidable on it; the defect is not the amount charged but that the waiting period the amount pays for was never completed.

No POL-NS-09 trigger fires, so this dispute should be resolved now with a refund rather than held for a human reviewer: neither party shows any counterparty dispute in the trailing 90 days (both 0), and the rider's trailing-30-day no-show dispute count is 0. The deciding fact — the driver's dwell — is carried by a COMPLETE artifact at weight 1.0, so confidence is not capped below the 0.70 floor and no escalation limb is available.

The driver is owed nothing, notwithstanding his statement that he waited 'at the marked bay'. I accept that his position is corroborated — the trace puts him about 24 m from the pin, well inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, so this is not a POL-NS-03 wrong-face-of-the-venue case — but POL-NS-07 pays compensation only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and limb (c) is not satisfied. A 240-second hold against a 300-second minimum earns no compensation, and the SGD 8.00 sits with the rider as a refund.

The driver did arrive at the pickup point on the platform's own geofence test. The GPS trace for this trip carries 25 consecutive position fixes, every one of them about 24 m from the Plaza Singapura ride-hail bay pin (min 24.01 m, max 24.01 m, mean 24.01 m), so the driver sat far inside the 120 m arrival radius that POL-NS-02 prescribes for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, and the trip record independently carries a driver 'arrived' event. Limbs (a) and (b) of POL-NS-01 are made out; arrival is not in dispute on this record.

The arrival marker is not a false one within POL-NS-05. The driver's track holds a single unbroken interval at 0.0 km/h, with no excursion and no sampling gap, so at the moment the 'arrived' event was recorded the driver was stationary 24 m from the pin and not travelling on any road. No false-arrival referral can arise against this driver, and the rider cannot use POL-NS-05 to attack the marker.

The rider was not at the pickup point. The rider's own track in the same trace places the rider's device about 519 m from the pin across all 11 of its fixes, with zero qualifying fixes inside the 150 m rider-presence radius for LARGE_VENUE. Limb (c) of POL-NS-04 is therefore affirmatively failed on admissible fixes, and the rider cannot be exonerated under that clause on the claim that the rider was at the pin and waiting.

The rider never sent a locating or coordinating message. The chat log holds exactly three messages - the system notice 'Your driver has arrived' and two messages from the driver ('At the mall ride-hail bay.' and 'I have to cancel now.') - and nothing from the rider. Limb (a) of POL-NS-04 fails for want of any message from the rider, so the rider-contact route to exoneration is closed regardless of what the rider now asserts.

This is a driver reporting an absent rider, not a driver admitting he could not find one. The trip was terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW - one of the three codes POL-NS-01 limb (d) recognises - and the trip record shows no boarding event anywhere. Had the code been DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE the case would be removed to POL-NS-03; it is not.

The amount charged reconciles with the fee schedule. The SGD 8.00 cancellation line is the vehicle-tier fee fixed for RYDE_XL and is the greater of that figure and the SGD 4.00 LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee, which is exactly what the schedule's resolution rule prescribes. There is therefore no fare defect under POL-NS-08(d) and no basis to discount the bundle on that ground.

There is no anti-farming pattern to answer for. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the absolute threshold of 4, and 1 over driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 120 is a rate of 0.008, far below the 0.08 threshold, so the POL-NS-07 check does not trip: compensation is not withheld on that ground and no POL-NS-09(d) escalation lies against this driver.

I do not overstate the dwell, and I do not ask the tribunal to read the minimum differently. The trace's own arithmetic gives the driver 240 seconds of continuous stationary presence inside the geofence against the 300-second minimum for LARGE_VENUE - a 60-second shortfall - and if POL-NS-06 is applied to that arithmetic the cancellation-fee line does not stand; the driver does not dispute it. What the driver asks of the ruling is that it record this as a one-minute timing defect and not as driver misconduct: the driver was present, stationary and willing at the correct bay, the rider was 519 m away and silent, the rider's remedy is confined to the SGD 8.00 fee line, and no adverse finding, referral or escalation follows.

ruling.explanation:
The SGD 8.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full. Both sides agree on the decisive numbers, and the artifacts back them: the driver's GPS trace shows a single continuous stationary hold inside the Plaza Singapura ride-hail geofence from 17:15:00 to 17:19:00 — 240 seconds — and the trip record shows the driver cancelled at 17:19:00. POL-NS-01(c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least 300 seconds for a LARGE_VENUE pickup before a no-show fee becomes chargeable, and the hold was 60 seconds short. Arrival itself is not in issue: the trace places the driver about 24 m from the pin, well inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE radius, and the arrival marker is not a false one under POL-NS-05 (stationary, 0.0 km/h, no 300 m or 15 km/h trigger), so nothing turns on that clause for either party. POL-NS-06 makes the shortfall a strict-liability refund: the fee is returned in full whether or not the rider was present or responsive, so the driver's presence and willingness — which the trace fully corroborates — do not save the charge. The driver cannot bridge the gap by summing separate in-geofence intervals under POL-NS-06(i): the trace contains only one such interval (run_count 1), and the traffic advisory for this pickup road and window is a MISSING artifact (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so limb (i) has nothing to operate on in any event. The driver's request that the 60-second shortfall be recorded as a one-minute timing defect rather than misconduct is accepted: nothing here treats him as having farmed the fee, and no adverse finding, referral or escalation follows. The rider's rider-contact argument under POL-NS-04 fails on its own terms (no rider message in the chat, and the rider's track sits about 519 m from the pin), but the rider does not need it — the refund flows from the driver's dwell, not from her conduct. Driver compensation is not payable: POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full, and limb (c) is not. The amount refunded is the cancellation-fee line, which is the whole contested SGD 8.00; it reconciles with the fee schedule (the greater of the SGD 4.00 zone-class fee and the SGD 8.00 RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee), so no fare defect under POL-NS-08(d) and no bundle discount applies. No POL-NS-09 escalation limb fires: the arrival event sits on a GPS fix at the same instant, the trace carries 25 fixes with no gap across the waiting window, the chat holds exactly the 3 messages the trip record reports, neither party shows a counterparty dispute in the trailing 90 days, and the rider's trailing-30-day no-show dispute count is 0.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
